headline: Japan Core CPI Rises 2.1% in September, Supporting Rate Hike Expectations
summary: Japan's core consumer price index rose 2.1% year over year in September, matching forecasts, while the index excluding fresh food and energy gained 2.4% ahead of the Bank of Japan's policy meeting.
why: The Bank of Japan is normalizing monetary policy after decades of ultra-easy settings, affecting global bond yields and the Japanese yen.

impacts.name: Japanese Yen
impacts.why: Inflation staying above the 2% target increases the likelihood of an interest rate increase by the Bank of Japan.

impacts.name: Japanese Banking
impacts.why: Prospects of monetary tightening support net interest margins for Japanese domestic lenders.

why_moved: Core inflation matching expectations and remaining above the Bank of Japan's target reinforced trader expectations of near-term interest rate increases.
